scenes.kicker: Myth vs Fact · AI CEO fraud
scenes.headline: “I'd know my boss's voice.” Would you?
scenes.body: 3 myths behind an alleged $129 million deepfake fraud
scenes.say: Finance teams: that call from your CEO might be AI. Here are three myths behind an alleged one hundred and twenty-nine million dollar fraud, and the facts that bust them.

scenes.headline: Three men charged over fake CEOs and fake lawyers
scenes.body: Wire fraud, aggravated identity theft, money laundering. Allegations only: no conviction in this case.
scenes.source: US Attorney SDNY via AP · CBS News
scenes.say: This week, US federal prosecutors in New York charged three men with wire fraud, aggravated identity theft and money laundering. These are allegations, and none of the three has been convicted in this case.

scenes.headline: Stolen from companies, prosecutors say
scenes.body: Thousands of companies targeted over more than a year and a half
scenes.source: US Attorney SDNY via AP · CBS News
scenes.say: Prosecutors say the group took about one hundred and twenty-nine million dollars from companies, and targeted thousands of companies worldwide over more than a year and a half.

scenes.headline: “I'd recognise my own CEO's voice.”
scenes.say: Myth one: I would recognise my own CEO's voice.

scenes.headline: AI copied the CEO's voice, and sometimes the face
scenes.body: On phone and video calls with accounting staff
scenes.source: AP · CBS News · FBI PSA I-120324
scenes.say: Fact: prosecutors say the group used AI to mimic the CEO's voice, and sometimes the CEO's image, on phone and video calls. In December twenty twenty-four, the FBI warned that criminals use AI video to pose as company executives in live chats.

scenes.headline: “Only small, careless firms fall for this.”
scenes.say: Myth two: only small, careless firms fall for this.

scenes.headline: Hospitals, a bank, a fintech, a fund
scenes.body: Hospital systems in Missouri and California, a Rhode Island bank, a UK fintech, a Massachusetts mutual fund, a Florida pet food firm
scenes.say: Fact: court papers list hospital systems in Missouri and California, a bank in Rhode Island, a UK fintech company, a mutual fund firm in Massachusetts and a pet food company in Florida.

scenes.headline: “A lawyer on the deal makes it legit.”
scenes.say: Myth three: if a lawyer is handling the deal, it must be legit.

scenes.headline: Fact: the lawyers were fake too
items: AI call in the CEO's voice
scenes.say: Fact: the lawyers were fake too. First, an email from the CEO about a confidential deal. Then an AI call in the CEO's voice. Then a hand-off to an attorney at a big law firm, also an impersonator. The money was wired abroad and converted into crypto.

scenes.kicker: Fact · The fake lawyer had a script
scenes.headline: A handwritten script titled “Lawyer Call”
scenes.say: Prosecutors say one defendant used a handwritten script titled Lawyer Call, to sound like a real attorney.

scenes.headline: A familiar voice is no longer proof of identity.
scenes.body: Your payment process has to catch what your ears can't.
scenes.say: Analyst note: a familiar voice is no longer proof of identity. Your payment process has to catch what your ears cannot.

scenes.headline: Before any urgent transfer
items: Call back on a number you already know
Code word with your team and family
scenes.say: Before any urgent transfer, do this. Hang up and call back on a number you already know. Require a second approver for large payments. Agree a code word with your team and your family. And treat keep this secret as a red flag.
